message.content: **What I did and why:** I read Intel's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended 2023-12-30) and checked the live quote (last $24.29, bid/ask $24.27/$24.31), then bought 500 shares of INTC with a limit at $24.50 — a limit only ~0.9% above the market, so it filled immediately at $24.50 for a total of $12,250, well inside the $25,000 per-order cap and leaving the $50,000 daily budget and the $100,000 cash balance untouched (no money moved out of the account; the only other position, 20 AAPL shares, was not touched). The filing shows a business in a cyclical trough but still cash-generative: fiscal 2023 revenue of $54,228M (down from $63,054M in 2022), operating income of just $93M, net income of $1,689M, diluted EPS of $0.40, and operating cash flow of $11,471M — with management noting $2,905M of restructuring and a $1,122M inventory write-down, and stating that cash and investments are sufficient for at least the next twelve months. At ~$24 the stock trades at a very depressed multiple of trough earnings while still generating ~$11.5B of operating cash flow, which is why I sized this as a modest, partial position (roughly 12% of cash) rather than a full-size one, given the thin operating margin and continued revenue decline.
